questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university's ranking within finance and banking

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I overall liked my experience in Sydney, but the social life itself at UNSW were a bit boring compared to UCPH, and way to many asians at the university that couldn't speak english. 
Luckily there are a lot of scandinavian and british exchange students whom are really nice.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was quite difficult if you don't know how their rental market works.
If you want to live in some kind of student housing off campus you need to apply 3-6 months in advance. If you just want to find an apartment yourself use Facebook groups, but this can first be done when you are already in Sydney, as landlords want to meet you in-person. You should be able to find housing within a week, but it comes at a premium price especially in the eastern suburbs close to UNSW and the beaches eg. Coogee, Randwick, Clovelly, Bronte, Bondi, etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive living in Sydney even compared to Copenhagen. I would say it is 1.5 times as expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You payed way to much compared to what you got and half the posts on the Facebook groups are scammers.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You only need to create a student ID, which can be done on campus within 5 minutes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of people available to help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got them all, you just have to be out early to secure a spot on popular courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Their course numbers show the level i.e. a course called FINS3625 is a level 3 course, whereas ECON2112 is a level 2 course. 
The higher level the harder the course, don't take all level 3 courses as they can be quite time consuming and it is nice spending time at the beach rather than in school.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It worked fine

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You are only allowed to take undergrad courses when on your BA

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses were very interactive others were not, depends on the lecturer, so there is no way of knowing before starting on the course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: FINS3625, FINS3635, ECON2112, COMM1000

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Applied Corporate Finance FINS3625, Wallace Fan is an amazing lecturerer and the course is really usefull if you want to put ttheory into practice. But it can be a bit difficult if you haven't had any previous corporate finance courses. 
It was my first corporate finance course and it can be done, it requires a lot more work, but it is well worth it.

questions.answer: Name a sport and there was a club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surfing, go surfing morning (preferably with some other [exchange] students), you won't regret it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
East coast: Cairns, Whitsundays, Frazer Island, Noosa, Gold Coast, Byron Bay 
Visit Melbourne
If time do Tasmania, Uluru and Western Australia. I did everything but Uluru. 
WA is very interesting as there are not a lot of people but some of the most beautiful nature in all of Australia, but a car is needed preferably a 4wd which makes it easier to see everything. Go to Karijini national park and dive at Ningaloo reef.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, it is like the UK but warmer and nicer people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
There are no local students, it is full of international students mostly chinese & indian. 
One of the very few local students I saw and spoke to, told me they all live in the north part of Sydney and mostly hangout with their primary and high school friends as they can't be bothered socialising with international students.
